blocks.html: HA–protein recognition is the best-quantified of the three systems and is the textbook example of combining aromatic CH–π stacking + carboxylate salt bridges + H-bonds in a shallow, calcium-independent groove (the Link module fold).

The Link-module/HABD binds an HA octasaccharide in a shallow groove. From the murine CD44 HABD–HA crystal structures (Banerji et al., Nat. Struct. Mol. Biol. 2007; PDB 2JCQ/2JCR); human numbering given first:

items: Arg41 (mouse Arg45) is the single most critical residue — it forms a salt bridge/H-bond to the HA GlcA carboxylate and reorients between two conformers (ordered "type A"/apo vs "partially disordered/type B" HA-bound), the basis of affinity regulation and mechanical force-sensing.

Tyr42 (Tyr46), Arg78 (Arg82), Tyr79 (Tyr83) form a contiguous patch; the Tyr residues provide CH–π stacking against the apolar sugar faces and the Arg residues provide electrostatic/H-bond contacts to the carboxylate and ring oxygens.

Additional contacts: Asn25, Lys38, Lys68, Asn100/Asn101, Tyr105, His101; plus peripheral basic residues (Arg150, Arg154, Lys158, Arg162) from the N-/C-terminal link extensions that provide two alternative binding registers (mode-1/mode-2). Thirteen residues make prominent contacts: Arg41, Tyr42, Cys77, Arg78, Tyr79, Ile88, Asn94, Ile96, Cys97, Ala98, Ala99, His101, Tyr105.
Ile88/Ile96/Ala98/Ala99 contribute van der Waals/hydrophobic packing (Cys77/Cys97 form a structural disulfide, not an HA contact).

Affinity: CD44–HA is intrinsically low-affinity (single-site Kd in the µM to tens-of-µM range), with physiological avidity from multivalent HMW-HA and receptor clustering; binding requires a minimum HA hexa-/octasaccharide.

sections.title: TSG-6 Link module (Link_TSG6) — highest-affinity Link module

blocks.html: NMR/crystal work (Kohda et al. Cell 1996; Mahoney et al. JBC 2001; Blundell et al. JBC 2003):

items: Key HA-binding residues line a shallow groove and the β4/β5 loop: Lys11, Tyr12, His45, Tyr59, Lys63, Phe70, Tyr78, Arg81 (with Asn67, Lys72, Asp77, Glu86 and Trp88 also implicated). The aromatic residues Tyr59, Phe70, Tyr78 (and Tyr12) stack (CH–π) against the HA sugar rings; Lys11, Lys63, Lys72, Arg81 form electrostatic/H-bond contacts to the GlcA carboxylate; Asn67 H-bonds; a ligand-induced conformational change in the β4/β5 loop accompanies binding.

Affinity/thermodynamics:ScienceDirectITC gives Kd ~0.2–0.5 µM for HA oligomers (HA6–HA8; HA4 does not bind), the interaction being exothermic with favorable entropy — a thermodynamic profile typical of GAG–protein binding. TSG-6 binds HA ~an order of magnitude more tightly than CD44.

Trp51 and Trp88 form the hydrophobic core (Trp88 near the binding surface); the Link module fold is locked by two conserved disulfides (in human TSG-6, C58–C127 and C82–C103 within the Link-module region) — essential for the fold, not HA contacts.

sections.title: General amino-acid grammar for HA (and the three-way comparison)

items: CH–π/aromatic stacking: Tyr (over-represented in HA sites) and Trp stack against the apolar faces of GlcNAc and GlcA; His can contribute. Per Asensio/Jiménez-Barbero (Acc. Chem. Res. 2013), experimental stacking free energies in water are ~1–2 kcal/mol per interaction (gas-phase QM 3–8, up to −12 kcal/mol for tight geometries), driven by dispersion tuned by electrostatics (C–H polarization by ring O and by the electron-withdrawing acetamido/carboxylate) and a hydrophobic/desolvation contribution. Trp is favored for its large, electron-rich, polarizable indole; Tyr adds an H-bonding OH. Removing the aromatic (galectin-3 W181→M) abolishes binding; W181Y/F cost ~1.1 kcal/mol, W181H ~3.3 kcal/mol (JACS Au 2024). Typical stacking geometry ~3.5–4.5 Å between ring plane and sugar CH.

Hydrogen bonding: Asn, Gln, Asp, Glu, Arg, Lys, Ser, Thr, Tyr, His side chains and backbone amides make cooperative bidentate H-bonds to the GlcNAc N-acetyl (accepting carbonyl + donating NH), the GlcA carboxylate, ring O5, and hydroxyls; water-mediated H-bonds are common (typical O···O/N···O 2.7–3.2 Å).

Ionic: the GlcA carboxylate–Arg/Lys salt bridge is the defining polar-ionic contact for HA (Arg41 in CD44; Arg81/Lys11/Lys63/Lys72 in TSG-6); the polyanionic chain also recruits basic patches for electrostatic steering.
Hydrophobic/van der Waals: Ala/Ile/Leu/Val/Pro pack against sugar CH arrays and the GlcNAc N-acetyl methyl (which frequently sits in a hydrophobic pocket).

Disulfides: structurally essential for the Link module (CD44/TSG-6 conserved S–S), C-type lectin folds, and antibody Fv — never a direct sugar contact. HA-binding Link modules are calcium-independent (unlike C-type lectins).

Sulfur–sugar contacts: documented in other systems — Met sulfur can make S···π and S···H–C contacts with sugar faces (Met-aromatic interactions worth ~0.3–0.5 kcal/mol;PubMedMet sulfur behaves as an electrophile toward electron-rich atoms), and Cys/Met can H-bond to sugar OH; these are minor for HA specifically.

Multivalency / glycoside cluster effect: single-site GAG/lectin affinities are weak (µM–mM); biological avidity comes from HMW-HA presenting many sites to clustered receptors — entropy/enthalpy compensation is characteristic.

o26.label: O26
o26.name: O-antigen · E. coli
o26.structureNote: Trisaccharide repeat unit — α-L-Rha, α-L-FucNAc, β-D-GlcNAc

blocks.html: Anti-O-polysaccharide antibodies and O-antigen-specific tailspike proteins characteristically bind 1–2 repeat units in a shallow groove or pocket:

items: CH–π stacking: the apolar B-face/α-face of the sugar rings — especially the pyranose ring of L-Rha (whose C6 methyl and axial CH array make a strongly hydrophobic patch) and the methyl-bearing face of L-FucNAc (6-deoxy sugar) — are expected to stack against Trp/Tyr in the combining site. Deoxy sugars (Rha, Fuc/FucNAc) are prime CH–π partners because they present large apolar CH surfaces.

Hydrogen bonding: the two N-acetyl groups (on GlcNAc and FucNAc) offer both a H-bond-accepting carbonyl and a donating amide NH; hydroxyls at Rha O2/O3/O4 and GlcNAc O4/O6 pair with Asn/Asp/Glu/Arg/Gln side chains and backbone amides in the bidentate/cooperative patterns typical of carbohydrate recognition.
Hydrophobic/van der Waals: the N-acetyl methyls of GlcNAc/FucNAc and the C6 methyls of Rha/FucNAc insert into apolar pockets lined by Ala/Val/Leu/Ile/Pro/Trp.
No ionic contacts to the sugar are expected (the O26 O-antigen is neutral) — distinguishing it sharply from HA and PG.

Disulfides: as in all IgG Fv domains, the intradomain VH/VL disulfides are essential for the fold but do not contact sugar. The nearest structural analogues for the L-configured galacto-type sugars are L-fucose/L-galactose lectins (e.g. Aspergillus fumigatus AFL with L-galactopyranose, PDB 4D52; Ulex europaeus UEA-II, PDB 1QOT) — useful only as qualitative modeling surrogates, not O26-specific.

blocks.html: PG recognition splits between the glycan (aromatic-stacking–dominated, as in lysozyme/LysM) and the peptide stem (H-bond/salt-bridge/shape-dominated, as in PGRPs, NOD, vancomycin).
Six subsites A–F bind the GlcNAc/MurNAc hexasaccharide; catalytic residues Glu35 (general acid) and Asp52. Key aromatic/H-bond contacts:

items: Trp62 in subsite B stacks (CH–π) against the nonpolar face of the sugar ring and H-bonds via its indole to a sugar hydroxyl (O6 in subsite C); its indole rotates toward subsite C on binding. Mutants Trp62→Tyr/Phe/Gly alter the binding mode and (Trp62Gly, Trp62Tyr) convert the (GlcNAc)₃ inhibitor into a substrate, confirming Trp62’s combined stacking + H-bond role.
Trp63, Trp108 contribute additional stacking/hydrophobic contacts; Asp101 (subsites B/C) and Asn59/Ala107/Asn46 provide H-bonds. Human lysozyme replaces Trp62 with Tyr63.

blocks.html: Thermodynamically the interaction is enthalpy-driven H-bonding plus Trp stacking, with water-mediated H-bond networks.

Crystal structures of human PGRP-Iα C-terminal domain with a muramyl tripeptide (MurNAc-L-Ala-D-isoGln-L-Lys; PDB 1YCK, Guan et al. PNAS 2004) and with a muramyl pentapeptide (L-Ala-D-isoGln-L-Lys-D-Ala-D-Ala; PDB 2APH, Guan et al. Protein Sci. 2006) show the peptide stem buried at the deep end of a long groove, MurNAc in the middle, GlcNAc accommodated at the shallow end;PubMedthree conserved disulfides stabilize the PGRP fold (they do not touch ligand). Recognition is via H-bonds to the stem backbone and side chains plus van der Waals/shape complementarity; variable residues (e.g. the position corresponding to Tyr266 in PGRP-Iα / Tyr100 in Drosophila PGRP-SA) discriminate Lys-type vs DAP-type PG. Ligand-induced side-chain rearrangements lock the C-terminal D-Ala-D-Ala in place.Wiley Online LibraryBinding affinities are typically µM (SPR).

Ligand sensing occurs at the leucine-rich-repeat (LRR) concave surface. NOD1 is activated by iE-DAP-containing muropeptides with moderate affinity (~30 µM reported);ASM Journalsan isolated NOD2 LRR bound MDP with Kd ~212 nM (SPR; Grimes lab). No crystal structure of NOD1/NOD2 with ligand exists; a rabbit NOD2 LRR structure places a candidate Ser (S933) near the proposed binding region.PubMed CentralRecognition is thought to involve LRR inner-surface residues, but direct residue-level contacts are not yet crystallographically defined.

sections.title: Vancomycin — a peptide antibiotic, not a protein, but the paradigm of stem recognition

blocks.html: The glycopeptide’s rigid, cup-shaped aglycon forms five backbone–backbone hydrogen bonds to the acyl-D-Ala-D-Ala terminus (plus a water-mediated bridge),PDB-101with the Asn3 and N-methyl-Leu1 side chains framing the pocket. Vancomycin resistance (VanA/VanB) remodels the terminus to D-Ala-D-Lac, eliminating one critical H-bonduspto(a >1000-fold affinity loss). An N-acetyl-D-Ala-D-lactate analog has Kd >73 mM vs µM for D-Ala-D-Ala.

The stem peptide carries carboxylates (γ-D-Glu α-carboxyl; meso-DAP carboxyls) and, in DAP-type PG, the DAP amino group; these engage Arg/Lys/His in binding proteins and are the discriminating features between Lys-type and DAP-type PG for NOD1/NOD2 and PGRPs.
LD-transpeptidases use an active-site Cys nucleophile (covalent acyl-enzyme with the stem), a catalytic (not recognition) role. Otherwise disulfides serve fold stability (PGRPs).
